key_insight: Near full-SWAP coupling, distance from the singular point sets the preparation clock, while detuning direction shapes control geometry and can favor Dicke-state preparation.
engineering_relevance: The architecture enables multipartite state preparation using fixed global exchange couplings and local phase controls without measurement, but generic-coupling two-qubit gate costs exceed known Dicke circuits.
method: Interleave partial-SWAP collisions with local phase rotations in a differentiable control architecture.
Analyze invariant supports, fidelity ceilings, and preparation-time bounds at singular couplings.
Use numerical reachability certificates, fidelity optimization, and near-full-SWAP slow-time theory.
evidence_signal: Numerical certificates support full-sector reachability for sampled couplings up to dimension 21; optimizations exceed 0.999 fidelity up to dimension 1716, and near-full-SWAP Dicke preparation is 2–5× faster than at a generic coupling at detuning 0.1 in sectors of dimension 70–252.
watch_item: The near-full-SWAP speedup is target-dependent: other tested target families are delayed, and singular couplings impose exact reachability restrictions.
paper_title: Differentiable collision-model control for multipartite state engineering: reachability, geometry, and preparation cost
